questions.q: Why does this lesson say governance 'concentrates' on the semantic model rather than on individual reports?
options: A single semantic model can feed many reports, so RLS, OLS, labels, and refresh health there affect everything built on top of it
Reports cannot have any settings of their own in Power BI
Governance only applies to semantic models, never to reports or dashboards
Semantic models are always stored in a separate, more secure workspace
questions.explain: Because one semantic model can underlie many downstream reports, governance controls defined on the model (RLS, OLS, sensitivity, refresh) have a wide blast radius — good or bad — across everything built on it.

questions.q: What is required for a semantic model to connect to an on-premises data source for refresh, that is NOT required for a purely cloud-based source?
options: A gateway connection
A Power BI Premium capacity
A sensitivity label
Object-level security
questions.explain: On-premises or VNet data sources require a gateway connection to refresh; cloud-only sources don't need one, though a gateway can still be used for enhanced connection control.

questions.q: What happens if a data source's password changes but the semantic model's stored credentials are never updated?
options: Scheduled refresh starts failing silently until someone notices and updates the credentials
Power BI automatically detects and updates the new password
The semantic model is automatically deleted after repeated failures
Nothing changes — stored credentials are not affected by source password changes
questions.explain: Credentials are entered once and retained with the model. If the source password changes without updating them here, refresh fails silently until someone investigates and updates Data source credentials.

questions.q: Besides refresh, which other governance-relevant controls live in a semantic model's Settings pane?
options: Sensitivity label, Endorsement, and Sharing/Data access
Tenant settings and domain assignment
Workspace naming conventions only
Nothing else — Settings is exclusively for refresh configuration
questions.explain: The same Settings pane also exposes Sensitivity label (Lesson 10), Endorsement (later in the course), and Sharing/Data access including RLS roles (Lessons 7 and 9).

questions.q: According to this lesson's checklist, what should happen before calling a semantic model 'production-ready'?
options: Refresh schedule set and history checked, credentials current with a named owner, and owner/sensitivity label set before downstream reports are built
The model must be converted to DirectQuery mode
The model must be published to at least five different workspaces
All tenant settings must be set to 'Enabled for the entire organization'
questions.explain: The checklist covers verifying the refresh schedule is actually working (not just configured), ensuring credentials have a responsible owner, and setting ownership/sensitivity labels before downstream reports proliferate.
